prompt: Pull together the messages about infrastructure incidents from the channels where a member named Robert is a full workspace member, not a guest, and tell me his role there.
binding_note: Only a first name is given, so 'Robert' resolves to two workspace members: Robert Walsh (admin role, member of general/random/engineering) and Robert Chen (member role, member of core-infra/model-research/product-growth/frontend/project-alpha-dev). A third Robert (Robert Kim, guest role) is excluded by the same workspace-membership filter even though his channel and topic otherwise match, because guest is not a full workspace role.

obligations.name: infra_incident_messages_by_robert_channel
obligations.description: Messages discussing infrastructure incidents located inside channel(s) where a user first-named Robert holds conversation membership AND that same user's workspace_membership role is not guest; the referent Robert is not resolved between the two matching non-guest users.
obligations.scope: messages in channels where a user first-named Robert holds conversation membership and a non-guest workspace_membership role, restricted to infrastructure-incident content

obligations.name: robert_workspace_membership_pair
obligations.description: The displayed workspace-membership pair (which Robert, and his non-guest role) tied to whichever channel set was used above, since the owner/admin/member distinction on the membership must be reported rather than assumed.
obligations.scope: workspace_membership role for whichever Robert anchors the selected channel/message set

task_spec.text: Gather the infrastructure-incident messages found in the channel(s) belonging to a non-guest workspace member named Robert.
Alongside those messages, report which Robert it is and his workspace membership role for that channel.

access_plan: Use users.list to find all users whose real_name/display_name contains 'Robert' (Robert Walsh, Robert Chen, Robert Kim). For each, check workspace role via their user_teams/workspace_membership record and discard any with role=guest (excluding Robert Kim). For the remaining candidates, use users.conversations to enumerate their conversation memberships, then conversations.history on each of their channels to locate messages whose text concerns infrastructure incidents (outages, memory pressure, login failures, budget overruns). Present the membership pair (user, role) alongside the selected channel's messages without collapsing the two non-guest candidates into one.
